Thanks Emily — this is perfect and very helpful. Below are two illustrative pricing structures mapped to your 100M tokens/month baseline. Numbers are back-of-envelope but designed to hit your $/1M target and budget range; we’ll formalize in the quote.

Option A — Annual license + per-token pricing (recommended for predictable growth)
- Annual license: $48,000/year (billed annually) → ≈ $4,000/mo amortized
- Committed baseline: 100M tokens/month included
- Overages: $10 per 1M tokens over baseline
- Support: Standard (business-hours) included

Example math (100M baseline):
- License amortized: $4,000/mo
- Token unit cost (baseline included): effectively spreads into license; if you consume 100M, incremental cost = $0 beyond license for baseline; overages at $10/1M
- If you exceed baseline by 50M in a month: overage = 50 * $10 = $500 (note tokens counted in 1M units)

Option B — Reserved capacity / flat monthly (reserved pool, simpler billing)
- Flat reserved fee: $12,000/mo for capacity up to 200M tokens/month
- Includes Standard support
- No per-token overages within cap; overages billed at $9/1M

Notes on hosted vs private unit economics: hosted API typically has higher per-token unit costs but lower up-front license; Private/VPC has license + lower marginal token costs and gives you dedicated control/throughput. We can run a simple model on your historical distribution and show total monthly cost under each plan.

Support tier add-ons (Marissa — more detail attached in SOW template):
- Premium support: +$3,500/mo (24/7, 4-hour P1, TAM)
- Enterprise: custom (onsite reviews, custom SLAs)

Attachments: SOW_template.docx (attached)

If this looks reasonable, I’ll convert Option A into a formal quote (line-items + legal) and include the SOW and DocuSign. Want to meet Tue/Wed to finalize?

Thanks,
Ben

- Premium (+$3,500/mo): 24/7 coverage; 4-hour initial response for P1; includes a Technical Account Manager (weekly syncs) and runbooks for on-call.

Environment guidance:

Operational notes:

- Backup/retention and key management (KMS) options will be included as configurable line items.

Next steps: Ben will produce the quote for Option A (license + overages) and Option B (flat reserved). I’ll include the Premium support line item as optional.
